public_prompt: Two annotators labelled 3,000 conversations for whether the issue was settled. They match on 88%, so the label set was declared reliable, and a classifier at 87% was declared close to the ceiling those labels allow. The route being taken: 88% match means reliable labels. Report whether the label set supports the ceiling claim.
observable_resources: labels/match.csv — 3,000 double-labelled items; the two annotators match on 88.0%; the majority label is applied to 91% of items
labels/tiebreak.md — where the two differ, annotator A's label is kept; there is no third pass
labels/annotator-marginals.csv — annotator A applies the majority label to 94% of items, annotator B to 87%
labels/audit-sample.md — a 100-item audit by a subject expert disagrees with the kept label on 23 items, 19 of them A's
closure:classifier-acceptance — closed; accepts the classifier at 87% as close to the label ceiling
closure:annotator-contract-terms — closed; sets the annotators' pay and hours; rests on the supplier contract, not on how their labels compare
closure:conversation-data-handling — closed; fixes how conversations may be stored and who may read them; rests on the privacy assessment, not on the quality of the labels

protected_gold.root_success_rubric: PASS iff annotator match is corrected for the agreement two annotators would reach by chance given the 91% majority label — showing it is barely above chance — the answer identifies that differences are settled by keeping one annotator's label rather than by a further pass, and it refuses the ceiling claim. FAIL if the answer accepts 88% as support for reliability, compares the classifier against the same labels without questioning them, or only recommends more annotators.

source_provenance: no external dataset; every figure is authored for this benchmark and is not an empirical finding
notes: A solver that keeps the raw-match framing accepts the ceiling claim; two annotators who both apply the majority label about 90% of the time match on 88% with no shared competence at all.
